On this node (4× RTX 3090, 2× EPYC 7763) it reaches about **5.1 TFLOPS at N=16384** and **4.1–4.3 TFLOPS at N=8192** with 4 ranks. The original serial code runs at 0.17 GFLOPS (N=2048 took 99.8 s). Only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` changed, the executable is still `matmul`, and the command-line options and output format are the same.\n\n**How the work is split**\n- **MPI:** the rows of C are divided evenly among the ranks. B is a fixed formula, so each rank generates it locally and nothing needs to be broadcast. Each finished row chunk is sent to rank 0 while computation is still running, instead of in one gather at the end. That gather had been taking up to 3.7 s at N=16384.\n- **CUDA:** one GPU per rank, preferring a GPU attached to the rank's own CPU socket. The FP64 kernel runs at about 93% of the RTX 3090's FP64 peak.\n- **OpenMP:** the CPU cores are worth using here, because these two EPYCs have more FP64 throughput than all four 3090s combined. Inside each rank, one thread drives the GPU and the other threads compute rows with a vectorized, cache-blocked kernel. Rows are handed to the GPU and CPU according to their measured speeds, so both finish at about the same time.\n\n**Correctness**\n- Validation passes for N from 1 to 16384, including non-aligned sizes like 7, 1000 and 12345, with 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 ranks and with 1–3 threads per rank.\n- Results are bit-identical no matter how many ranks or threads you use.\n- For powers of two the `-r` hash matches the original exactly. For other sizes the last bits differ: I use fused multiply-add throughout, while GCC compiled the original as a separate multiply and add. The values agree to about 1e-16 relative, so validation passes; if your external check compares hashes exactly, it will flag those sizes. Matching bit-for-bit would roughly halve GPU throughput on these cards, so I didn't.\n\n**Launching**\n- Use one rank per GPU, with each rank bound to its own cores, for example: `mpirun -np 4 --map-by ppr:2:socket:pe=32 ./matmul -n 16384`. Plain `mpirun -np 4` (Open MPI binds to socket) also works well.\n- With 2 or fewer ranks, Open MPI binds each rank to a single core by default, so the CPUs barely help (about 1.1 TFLOPS instead of 2.3–2.8). Add `--map-by socket --bind-to socket` in that case.\n- `OMP_NUM_THREADS` overrides the automatic thread count.\n- The build needs an MPI library with full thread support (`MPI_THREAD_MULTIPLE`, which Open MPI 4.1 here has). Without it, the program falls back to collecting results at the end, which is slower.\n\n`CMakeLists.txt` now finds MPI, OpenMP and the CUDA toolkit and compiles `matmul.cpp` as CUDA. It builds for common GPU generations (sm_70 to sm_90); add `-DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=native` to build only for the local GPUs.\n\nTimings on this machine varied by roughly ±10% because other users' jobs were running on it, so the figures above are best-of-several runs."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":103,"cache_read_input_tokens":200318,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":103},"output_tokens":3,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"23ef5711-b380-4369-80ed-fec3d7689ff2","uuid":"2d09d601-3292-4d58-be89-340766787c65","timestamp":"2026-10-06T06:05:28.868Z","request_id":"req_011CfkUnHVdHvLXDPB7nqAcn"}
